rules: verified=false means every signals field is null: such a child is a proposal only and must not become a rule.

surface=api: documented vendor API endpoint (scripts, integrations). The first-party web UI's own request paths are not documented and must not be assumed equal; web_ui_evidence says per service whether an official source links the web app to the API hosts.

web_ui_evidence (since wave 2): 'none', or an object whose uses_documented_api is 'same' (official source says the web client calls the documented API), 'partial' (official source puts the web client on the API host, paths not stated) or 'different' (official source shows the web client uses other hosts or paths), with the citation and a verbatim quote. A host overlap that needs two pages to see is not counted; it goes in web_ui_note.
host_sni lists names as the source spells them; a '*.' or '{...}' form is a pattern, not a literal.
transport is set for non-HTTP signals; those are invisible to an HTTP rule.
Hosts and paths are client assertions seen by a decrypting proxy, not authenticated identity.

Rows citing raw.githubusercontent.com, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, rubygems.org or api.nuget.org cite the vendor's own published spec, SDK, documentation repository or registry document, used where the vendor's documentation site was not reachable; each note names the file and its first single-quoted string is machine-checked to occur in the cited file. Third-party SDKs and packages whose vendor ownership could not be confirmed were rejected.
